speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see the newborn has increasing yellow discoloration of the eyes and skin. When did you first notice the yellowing, and has it spread from the face downwards to the chest and abdomen?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-week-old female newborn. The patient has been experiencing increasing yellow discoloration of her eyes and skin for 2 days. She was born at 39 weeks' gestation, initially weighed 3066 g and now weighs 3200 g. The patient is exclusively breastfed.

speaker: Doctor
text: Is she having at least three wet diapers and two stools per day, and are the stools yellow and seedy or pale/clay-colored? Has she been feeding well, and do you notice any dark urine?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Increasing yellow discoloration of the eyes and skin. I also have Exclusively breastfed, Brother died 3 months after liver surgery.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the family history of a sibling dying after liver surgery, I am concerned about a metabolic disorder like Galactosemia rather than simple breast milk jaundice. REQUEST TEST: Urine Reducing Substances

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: Serum Galactose-1-phosphate uridyltransferase (GALT) activity

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: Total and Direct Bilirubin Levels

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Total Bilirubin: 16.1 mg/dL, Direct Bilirubin: 0.7 mg/dL

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal GALT activity and normal urine reducing substances effectively rule out galactosemia, and the low direct bilirubin indicates unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia. Given the onset at two weeks in an exclusively breastfed infant with good weight gain and no signs of pathology, this is most consistent with breast milk jaundice. DIAGNOSIS READY: Breast milk jaundice
